workflows.title: Custom loop
workflows.template:
TASK TO LOOP ON:
Write an "LLM-as-a-Judge" evaluation prompt for a RAG pipeline. The judge must evaluate an AI's answer against retrieved context for "Contextual Faithfulness" (hallucination detection) and output a strict JSON with {"score": 1-5, "reasoning": "...", "hallucinated_spans": []}.

When working on this, run the following loop:

## GOAL
Simulate 3 complex RAG test cases: 1. A perfectly faithful answer. 2. A subtle hallucination (mixing real retrieved facts with fake numbers). 3. An answer that ignores the context entirely. Run your drafted Judge prompt against these 3 cases. Iterate and patch the Judge prompt's instructions until it correctly identifies the subtle hallucination without false positives and returns 100% valid JSON.

## EVALUATION CRITERIA
- All tests pass
- No linter or type errors

## IMPROVEMENT STRATEGY
Fix one failing check at a time, smallest change first.

## STOP CONDITIONS
- All evaluation criteria are met
- No improvement for 2 consecutive iterations
- Maximum of 5 iterations reached

## SAFETY RULES
- Never delete or overwrite files without explicit confirmation
- Stop and report if stuck, rather than guessing indefinitely
- Never fabricate test results — always show actual output

workflows.title: Root Cause Debugger
workflows.desc: Systematically trace a bug to its actual cause before proposing a fix.
workflows.template:
You are a methodical debugging partner. I have a bug in my {{language_or_stack}} code.

Symptom: {{symptom}}
What I expected: {{expected_behavior}}
Relevant code / error output:
{{code_or_error}}

Walk through this step by step:
1. List the most likely causes, ranked by probability.
2. Identify what evidence would confirm or rule out each one.
3. Ask me for any missing information before guessing.
4. Only propose a fix once the root cause is confirmed, not just the symptom.
Keep the fix minimal and isolated to the actual cause.
workflows.example: Filled with "Node.js / Express", a 500 error on file upload, and a stack trace — produces a ranked list of 3 likely causes before any fix is suggested.
practices: State the expected behavior, not just the error — it narrows the search fast
Paste the actual stack trace or logs, not a paraphrase
Ask the AI to rank causes before jumping to a fix

workflows.title: Error Trace Interpreter
workflows.desc: Turn a dense stack trace or log dump into a plain-language explanation and next steps.
workflows.template:
Act as a senior engineer reading this error trace for the first time.

Stack trace / log output:
{{trace}}

Environment: {{environment}}

1. Explain in plain language what actually failed and where.
2. Identify the single most likely trigger line in my code (not library internals).
3. List 2-3 concrete things to check next, in order.
Do not suggest a fix until the trigger is identified.
workflows.example: Paste a Python traceback + "Django 5, Postgres" — get a plain-language explanation of the failing line and 3 things to check.
practices: Include the full trace, not just the last line
Mention framework + version — error meanings shift between versions

workflows.title: Structured Code Review
workflows.desc: Get a thorough, standards-based review instead of a vague "looks good".
workflows.template:
You are a strict but fair code reviewer. Review the following {{language}} code for:
- Correctness and edge cases
- Security issues
- Readability and naming
- Performance concerns (only if material)

Code:
{{code}}

Constraints: {{constraints}}

Output format: a numbered list of issues, each with severity (blocker / suggestion / nit), the line it applies to, and a one-line fix. End with a short overall verdict.
workflows.example: Paste a PR diff with "no new dependencies" as a constraint — get issues tagged blocker/suggestion/nit with line references.
practices: Ask for severity tags so you know what to fix before merging
State constraints (style guide, no new deps) up front so suggestions stay usable

workflows.title: Refactor Proposal
workflows.desc: Get a concrete refactor plan with tradeoffs, not just rewritten code.
workflows.template:
You are refactoring the following {{language}} code for {{goal}} (e.g. readability, testability, performance).

Code:
{{code}}

Constraints: {{constraints}}

1. Identify the 2-3 biggest structural issues.
2. Propose a refactor plan as discrete, independently-shippable steps.
3. For each step, note the risk level and what could break.
4. Only show full rewritten code for the first step; describe the rest.
workflows.example: A 200-line function with "improve testability" as the goal — returns a 3-step plan with risk notes, code only for step one.
practices: Ask for a plan before a full rewrite — big diffs are hard to review safely
Request risk levels per step so you can stop after the safe ones

workflows.title: System Design Doc Draft
workflows.desc: Turn a rough feature idea into a structured design doc skeleton.
workflows.example: Feature: "rate limiting for public API" — returns a short doc with 2 alternatives (token bucket vs sliding window) and their tradeoffs.
practices: List non-goals explicitly — it stops the AI from over-scoping the design
Ask for alternatives with tradeoffs, not just one proposed approach

workflows.title: Tradeoff Analysis (ADR)
workflows.desc: Compare technical options in Architecture Decision Record format.
workflows.example: "Postgres vs DynamoDB for this service" — returns a pros/cons table and a recommendation tied to the stated read/write pattern.
practices: Name the real constraint (team size, existing infra) — it changes the right answer
Ask for the conditions that would flip the recommendation, not just one answer

workflows.title: Script Generator
workflows.desc: Generate a small, safe automation script with explicit guardrails.
workflows.example: "Bash script that renames files matching a pattern" — returns a script with a --dry-run flag and explicit error handling.
practices: Always ask for a dry-run mode on anything that touches files
Describe input/output shape precisely — vague specs produce scripts you have to rewrite

workflows.title: Repetitive Task Automator
workflows.desc: Turn a manual, repeated task into a reusable tool or snippet.
workflows.example: "Manually formatting PR descriptions from commit messages, daily" — returns a git alias or small script plus a one-line reason it beats a full app.
practices: Mention frequency — daily tasks justify more setup than monthly ones
Let the AI pick the automation type; over-specifying the format wastes its judgment

workflows.title: New Framework Onboarding
workflows.desc: Get a fast, practical ramp-up on an unfamiliar framework or tool.
workflows.template:
I'm an experienced {{background}} developer learning {{framework}} for the first time.

Goal: {{goal}} (e.g. ship a small feature, pass a review, evaluate for adoption)
Time available: {{time_available}}

Give me: the 5 core concepts I actually need (skip the rest), one thing that trips up people from my background specifically, and a minimal working example I can run today.
workflows.example: "React developer learning Svelte, to evaluate for adoption, 2 hours" — returns 5 core concepts and one React-specific gotcha.
practices: Name your existing background — it lets the AI skip what you already know
Set a time budget so the answer matches how deep you can actually go today

workflows.title: Concept Deep Dive
workflows.desc: Understand a specific technical concept at the right depth, with a check for understanding.
workflows.example: "Explain event loop, working knowledge, because I keep hitting race conditions in Node" — returns intuition, mechanics, a Node-specific example, and 2 check questions.
practices: Specify depth explicitly — "explain X" alone often returns either too shallow or too academic
State why you need it so the example lands in your actual context

workflows.title: Context Capsule for Tool Switch
workflows.desc: Carry full context when moving a task from one AI tool to another, without retyping everything.
workflows.template:
Summarize this conversation/task as a portable context capsule I can paste into another AI tool.

Include:
- The overall goal
- Key decisions already made and why
- Current state / what's been tried
- What's still unresolved
- Any constraints that must carry over

Keep it under 200 words and written so a different AI model can pick up the task with no other context.
workflows.example: Used at the end of a long Claude debugging session to hand the exact state off to ChatGPT or Copilot without losing decisions already made.
practices: Run this before switching tools, not after — it captures state while it's fresh
Ask for constraints explicitly; they're the thing most often lost in translation between tools

workflows.title: Session Handoff Summary
workflows.desc: Close out a work session with a summary your future self (or another tool) can resume from instantly.
workflows.template:
Write a handoff summary for this session on {{task_name}}.

Structure:
- Status: {{status}} (e.g. blocked, in progress, done pending review)
- What was completed
- What remains, in priority order
- Any open questions or decisions needed from me
- The exact next action to take when I resume

Write it for someone with zero memory of this session.
workflows.example: End-of-day summary for a migration task — next session opens with a precise "next action" instead of re-reading the whole thread.
practices: Write this at the end of every focus block, not just end of day
Always request an explicit "next action" line — it's the highest-value part
